thread:
maya: Heads up — trying to cut release 2024.6.3 but CI/promote job kept failing on artifact propagation. Blocking the cut window.

deploy-bot: [automated] promote-job failed: cache upload throttled, retries exhausted. Error snippet:
```
ERROR: upload failed: 429 Too Many Requests (PutObject)
  at uploader.uploadChunk (/srv/deploy/uploader.js:412)
  at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95)
Retries: 5/5, last-error-id=upload-7892
```

tyler: Seeing lots of concurrent s3/registry PUTs from the CI matrix this morning. Clients hammering the same bucket + no jitter on retries = burst that trips rate limits. Also a couple EPIPEs in the runner logs.

jen: Can we pin the release to the last-known-good artifact digest and manually promote to prod to unblock? Need ETA for the cut window.

alex: The last-good digest for the service image is `sha256:fa7b9c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b`. That's the one we promoted successfully in the previous cut. Manual promote should be possible if we avoid re-uploading blobs.

maya: If manual promote will avoid re-upload, I'm +1 to that so we don't waste the window. Can someone run it? Also open to short-term rollback if needed.

deploy-bot: Note: automatic promote triggers blob copy which re-GETs objects if not present. Manual promote with --force-digest uses existing registry blobs and should not trigger new uploads, but confirm image exists in target registry.

tyler: Confirmed blobs present in prod-registry for that digest. Manual promote will be a tag move mostly. I'd still recommend a temp mitigation on CI: reduce uploader concurrency and add jitter/backoff — otherwise we'll re-hit the same limit when we re-run tests.

jen: Decision proposal: 1) Manual promote to sha256:fa7b9... to unblock release. 2) Open incident and create a hotfix PR to reduce uploader concurrency + exponential backoff. 3) Post-cut follow-up to implement better rate-limiting at the CI-side.

maya: +1. Who can promote now?

alex: I can run it. Command I'll use: 
```
deploybot promote --source=staging --dest=prod --digest=sha256:fa7b9c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b --reason "manual-unblock-2024-06-13"
```

tyler: I'll open the hotfix PR and tag @jen for review. Patch will: set uploader.concurrency=2, add randomized jitter(0..500ms), and use exponential backoff on 429/503 errors.

deploy-bot: promote initiated by alex at 1718200301. Progress: copying tags, verifying blobs...
```
INFO: checking blobs... OK
INFO: moving tag from prod-candidate -> prod
SUCCESS: promoted digest sha256:fa7b9c1d... to prod at 2024-06-13T14:05:12Z
```

jen: Nice. Can someone update the release notes and CHANGELOG to reflect digest and the rollback instructions if there are regressions?

alex: Done — release notes updated in the draft: promoted digest, manual promote rationale, and rollback steps (`deploybot rollback --digest=previous-digest`). Also added a ticket to follow up on CI uploader improvements: INF-3245.

tyler: PR for uploader hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/984 — PTAL for expedited review.

ops-bot: Noted elevated PUT error rates and throttling in eu-west-1 between 13:50-14:10 UTC. Recommendation: throttle CI parallelism during next big cut until we deploy uploader backoff.

maya: Thanks all — release cut unblocked, proceeding with standard cut checklist. Post-cut action: monitor registry errors for 1h and keep the change window open for the uploader hotfix.

jen: I'll notify CS + PMs about the temporary pin and mitigations. :thumbsup:

alex: Will stay on call to monitor logs for the next 30m.

tyler: Merging hotfix once jen approves, then we'll schedule a follow-up deploy in the off-peak change window.

maya: Great. Closing thread after verification. :white_check_mark:
